description: email.rs:899: seen_threads.insert(tid.clone()) where tid is &Id borrowed from thread_map. Since seen_threads takes ownership and thread_map already holds the Id values, the clone is necessary here — Id does not implement Copy, and the borrow from thread_map prevents moving. This is a genuine Rust ownership constraint, not gratuitous cloning. However, rebuilding thread_map as HashMap<&Id, &Id> borrowing from the emails slice (which lives for the function's duration) would eliminate all Id allocations in the inner loop. Filing as a taste-level suggestion.
title: collapse_by_thread: tid.clone() on HashSet insert is avoidable
